Barcelona, ed. Gustavo Gili, 2002, p.133. p.136 12. Barja values the importance of the interweaving of light and shadow, presence and absence, distance and proximity. That is why in many of his works this ambiguous reality is constantly given, for example in Agulha no Palheiro (1988-89), where the spectator must find, among the pile of straw, a golden needle, referring to a well-known refrain that signals the difficulty of finding something, like a needle in a haystack. A needle that effectively exists is being retransmitted by an apparatus. In this piece it is indifferent whether one is sighted or not, only through touch is it possible to find it. The piece is precisely entitled instalação para nivelar visibilidades.
